correctness.rationale: For each integer n>=3 the hat Gram matrix is G=(4I+S+S^{-1})/6. Its inverse row is the periodic sum of b_j=sqrt(3)(-(2-sqrt(3)))^abs(j), solving the tridiagonal Green equation. Each continuous evaluation kernel is affine on cells and a convex combination of knot kernels; integrating its absolute value yields the stated F(a_j,a_{j+1}) and an attaining sign input. The infinite-line kernel has L1 norm exactly 2. Periodization cannot increase that norm, and specified opposite-sign overlapping translates cancel on a positive-measure interval for every finite odd/even n, making L_n<2. The reverse triangle inequality with geometric tails gives 0<2-L_n<=4sqrt(3)r^floor(n/2)/(1-r). Reproduction of constants and nontrivial sign changes yields L_n>1 and negativity defect (L_n-1)/2. An independently written exact rational cyclic-matrix computation recovered the n=3..12 values, including 16/9,17/9,257/132,2923/1485, all strictly below 2. The all-n statements follow from analytic Green-function/periodization proofs, not the finite experiment.

value.rationale: The sharp operator endpoint norm is the natural stability constant of a fundamental L2 spline orthoprojector. Complete rational norms for every mesh size, the finite strictness and exponential approach to a sharp constant, and exact positivity defect are useful independently of general nonsharp boundedness. This is a meaningful natural all-size classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice.

limitations: All-n bound derived analytically; finite checks only n=3..12.
